sanskrit: maitro 'tha śīlasaṃpannaḥ susahāyaparaś ca yaḥ muktaś ca vividhaiḥ saṅgais tasya pretya mahat phalam
english: The man who is friendly, endowed with good character, devoted to worthy companions, and freed from attachments of every kind—great is his reward in the world beyond.

sanskrit: suvṛttaḥ śīlasaṃpannaḥ prasannātmātmavid budhaḥ prāpyeha loke satkāraṃ sugatiṃ pratipadyate
english: Of good conduct, endowed with virtue, serene of soul, knower of the self, and wise—he wins honor here in this world and attains a happy course hereafter.

sanskrit: karma yac chubham eveha sadbhir ācaritaṃ ca yat tad eva jñānayuktasya muner dharmo na hīyate
english: Whatever auspicious deed is practiced here by the good—that very dharma of the sage endowed with knowledge never fails him.

sanskrit: niṣkramya vanam āsthāya jñānayukto jitendriyaḥ kālākāṅkṣī carann evaṃ brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: Having gone forth and taken up the forest, possessed of knowledge, his senses conquered, awaiting his hour and wandering thus, he becomes fit for union with Brahman.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ yasya bhūtebhyo bhūtānām abhayaṃ yataḥ tasya dehād vimuktasya bhayaṃ nāsti kutaś cana
english: He from whom no creature has anything to fear, and from whom creatures themselves have no fear—when he is released from the body, he has nothing whatever to dread.

sanskrit: avācinoti karmāṇi na ca saṃpracinoti ha samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu maitrāyaṇagatiś caret
english: He neither gathers up deeds nor heaps them together; impartial toward all beings, let him walk the path of universal friendship.

sanskrit: śakunīnām ivākāśe jale vāricarasya vā yathā gatir na dṛśyeta tathā tasya na saṃśayaḥ
english: As the track of birds in the sky or of creatures that move through water cannot be seen, so too is his course—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: gṛhān utsṛjya yo rājan mokṣam evābhipadyate lokās tejomayās tasya kalpante śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
english: He who, O king, casts off his household and attains to liberation alone—for him radiant worlds are made ready for everlasting years.

sanskrit: saṃnyasya sarvakarmāṇi saṃnyasya vidhivat tapaḥ saṃnyasya vividhā vidyāḥ sarvaṃ saṃnyasya caiva ha
english: Having renounced all works, having renounced austerity duly performed, having renounced the manifold branches of knowledge—having renounced, indeed, everything—

sanskrit: kāmeṣu cāpy anāvṛttaḥ prasannātmātmavic chuciḥ prāpyeha loke satkāraṃ svargaṃ samabhipadyate
english: and turning back no more toward the objects of desire, serene of soul, knower of the self, and pure—he wins honor here in this world and attains to heaven.

sanskrit: yac ca paitāmahaṃ sthānaṃ brahmarāśisamudbhavam guhāyāṃ pihitaṃ nityaṃ tad damenābhipadyate
english: And that station of the Grandsire, sprung from the mass of Brahman, hidden forever in the secret cave of the heart—that is reached through self-restraint.

sanskrit: jñānārāmasya buddhasya sarvabhūtāvirodhinaḥ nāvṛttibhayam astīha paraloke bhayaṃ kutaḥ
english: For one whose delight is in knowledge, who is awakened, at enmity with no living being, there is no fear of return to birth here—whence then any fear in the world beyond?

sanskrit: eka eva dame doṣo dvitīyo nopapadyate yad enaṃ kṣamayā yuktam aśaktaṃ manyate janaḥ
english: In self-restraint there is but a single flaw; a second is not to be found: that people take a man endowed with forbearance to be weak.

sanskrit: etasya tu mahāprājña doṣasya sumahān guṇaḥ kṣamāyāṃ vipulā lokāḥ sulabhā hi sahiṣṇunā
english: Yet from this very flaw, O greatly wise one, springs a far greater merit: by forbearance vast worlds are easily won by the patient man.

sanskrit: dāntasya kim araṇyena tathādāntasya bhārata yatraiva hi vased dāntas tad araṇyaṃ sa āśramaḥ
english: What need has the self-restrained man of the forest, and what use is it to the unrestrained, O Bhārata? Wherever the self-restrained may dwell, that very place is forest and hermitage to him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etad bhīṣmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ amṛteneva saṃtṛptaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ samapadyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this speech of Bhīṣma, King Yudhiṣṭhira, as though sated with the nectar of immortality, became filled with joy.

sanskrit: punaś ca paripapraccha bhīṣmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam tapaḥ prati sa covāca tasmai sarvaṃ kurūdvaha
english: And once more he questioned Bhīṣma, best of the upholders of dharma, concerning austerity; and he, O pride of the Kurus, told him all of it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvam etat tapomūlaṃ kavayaḥ paricakṣate na hy ataptatapā mūḍhaḥ kriyāphalam avāpyate
english: Bhīṣma said: All this, the seers declare, is rooted in austerity; for the fool who has practiced no austerity wins not the fruit of action.

sanskrit: prajāpatir idaṃ sarvaṃ tapasaivāsṛjat prabhuḥ tathaiva vedān ṛṣayas tapasā pratipedire
english: By austerity alone the Lord Prajāpati brought forth all this creation, and even so did the seers attain the Vedas through austerity.

sanskrit: tapaso hy ānupūrvyeṇa phalamūlānilāśanāḥ trīṃl lokāṃs tapasā siddhāḥ paśyanti susamāhitāḥ
english: By the gradual course of austerity, those who feed on fruit, root, and air, perfected by austerity and deeply composed, behold the three worlds.

sanskrit: auṣadhāny agadādīni tisro vidyāś ca saṃskṛtāḥ tapasaiva hi sidhyanti tapomūlaṃ hi sādhanam
english: Healing herbs, antidotes and the rest, and the three refined branches of knowledge—all succeed through austerity alone, for austerity is the root of every means.

sanskrit: yad durāpaṃ durāmnāyaṃ durādharṣaṃ durutsaham sarvaṃ tat tapasā śakyaṃ tapo hi duratikramam
english: Whatever is hard to win, hard to learn, hard to overcome, hard to endure—all of it can be achieved through austerity, for austerity is not to be surpassed.

sanskrit: surāpo 'saṃmatādāyī bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ tapasaiva sutaptena naraḥ pāpād vimucyate
english: The drinker of liquor, the taker of what is not given, the slayer of an embryo, the defiler of his teacher's bed—by austerity well performed a man is freed even from such sin.

sanskrit: tapaso bahurūpasya tais tair dvāraiḥ pravartataḥ nivṛttyā vartamānasya tapo nānaśanāt param
english: Austerity is of many forms, proceeding through this gate and that; yet for one who lives by withdrawal, there is no austerity higher than fasting.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ dānam indriyanigrahaḥ etebhyo hi mahārāja tapo nānaśanāt param
english: Non-injury, truthful speech, generosity, and the curbing of the senses—even beyond these, O great king, there is no austerity higher than fasting.

sanskrit: na duṣkarataraṃ dānān nātimātaram āśramaḥ traividyebhyaḥ paraṃ nāsti saṃnyāsaḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: There is nothing harder to do than giving, no order of life surpassing the householder's; beyond the threefold knowledge nothing is higher, and renunciation is the supreme austerity.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīha rakṣanti dhanadhānyābhiguptaye tasmād arthe ca dharme ca tapo nānaśanāt param
english: Men here guard the senses for the safeguarding of wealth and grain; therefore, for both prosperity and dharma, there is no austerity higher than fasting.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā manuṣyā mṛgasattamāḥ yāni cānyāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: Seers, ancestors, gods, men, the best of beasts, and whatever other beings there are, unmoving or moving—

sanskrit: tapaḥparāyaṇāḥ sarve sidhyanti tapasā ca te ity evaṃ tapasā devā mahattvaṃ cāpy avāpnuvan
english: all of them, devoted to austerity, attain perfection through austerity; and thus by austerity the very gods won their greatness.

sanskrit: imānīṣṭavibhāgāni phalāni tapasā sadā tapasā śakyate prāptuṃ devatvam api niścayāt
english: These cherished portions of reward are ever won through austerity; by austerity, assuredly, even godhood can be attained.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca satyaṃ dharme praśaṃsanti viprarṣipitṛdevatāḥ satyam icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Brahmins, seers, ancestors, and gods praise truth as the foundation of dharma. I wish to hear of truth; tell me of it, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: satyaṃ kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ rājan kathaṃ vā tad avāpyate satyaṃ prāpya bhavet kiṃ ca kathaṃ caiva tad ucyate
english: What are the marks of truth, O king, and how is it attained? Having attained truth, what comes of it, and how is it spoken of?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca cāturvarṇyasya dharmāṇāṃ saṃkaro na praśasyate avikāritamaṃ satyaṃ sarvavarṇeṣu bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: The confounding of the duties of the four orders is not commended; truth, most unchanging of all, holds good among all the orders, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: satyaṃ satsu sadā dharmaḥ satyaṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ satyam eva namasyeta satyaṃ hi paramā gatiḥ
english: Truth is ever the dharma of the good; truth is the eternal dharma. To truth alone should one bow, for truth is the supreme goal.

sanskrit: satyaṃ dharmas tapo yogaḥ satyaṃ brahma sanātanam satyaṃ yajñaḥ paraḥ proktaḥ satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: Truth is dharma, austerity, and yoga; truth is the eternal Brahman; truth is declared the highest sacrifice; in truth all things rest.

sanskrit: ācārān iha satyasya yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ lakṣaṇaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi satyasyeha yathākramam
english: I shall set forth here the observances of truth duly and in order, and the marks of truth as well, each in its turn.

sanskrit: prāpyate hi yathā satyaṃ tac ca śrotuṃ tvam arhasi satyaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ sarvalokeṣu bhārata
english: How truth is attained, that too you deserve to hear; truth is of thirteen kinds throughout all the worlds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: satyaṃ ca samatā caiva damaś caiva na saṃśayaḥ amātsaryaṃ kṣamā caiva hrīs titikṣānasūyatā
english: Truthfulness, impartiality, self-restraint—of this there is no doubt—freedom from envy, forbearance, modesty, endurance, absence of malice,

sanskrit: tyāgo dhyānam athāryatvaṃ dhṛtiś ca satataṃ sthirā ahiṃsā caiva rājendra satyākārās trayodaśa
english: renunciation, meditation, nobility, steadfastness ever firm, and non-injury, O lord of kings—these are the thirteen forms of truth.

sanskrit: satyaṃ nāmāvyayaṃ nityam avikāri tathaiva ca sarvadharmāviruddhaṃ ca yogenaitad avāpyate
english: Truth is imperishable, eternal, and likewise unchanging, and at variance with no dharma; this is attained through yoga.

sanskrit: ātmanīṣṭe tathāniṣṭe ripau ca samatā tathā icchādveṣakṣayaṃ prāpya kāmakrodhakṣayaṃ tathā
english: Impartiality toward what is dear to oneself, toward what is hateful, and toward an enemy alike—this is gained by reaching the extinction of liking and loathing, and likewise the extinction of desire and wrath.

sanskrit: damo nānyaspṛhā nityaṃ dhairyaṃ gāmbhīryam eva ca abhayaṃ krodhaśamanaṃ jñānenaitad avāpyate
english: Self-restraint is the perpetual absence of craving for another's goods, together with constancy, depth of character, fearlessness, and the stilling of anger; this is attained through knowledge.

sanskrit: amātsaryaṃ budhāḥ prāhur dānaṃ dharme ca saṃyamam avasthitena nityaṃ ca satyenāmatsarī bhavet
english: The wise call freedom from envy giving, and self-control in matters of dharma; by truth steadfastly maintained one becomes free from envy.

sanskrit: akṣamāyāḥ kṣamāyāś ca priyāṇīhāpriyāṇi ca kṣamate sarvataḥ sādhuḥ sādhv āpnoti ca satyavān
english: Between the pleasant and the unpleasant fruits of impatience and of forbearance, the good man forbears in every case; and the truthful man attains what is good.

sanskrit: kalyāṇaṃ kurute gāḍhaṃ hrīmān na ślāghate kva cit praśāntavāṅmanā nityaṃ hrīs tu dharmād avāpyate
english: The modest man does deep good yet never boasts of it; with speech and mind ever at peace—and modesty is won through dharma.

sanskrit: dharmārthahetoḥ kṣamate titikṣā kṣāntir ucyate lokasaṃgrahaṇārthaṃ tu sā tu dhairyeṇa labhyate
english: To forbear for the sake of dharma and gain is called endurance, which is patience; undertaken for the holding together of the world, it is won through steadfastness.

sanskrit: tyāgaḥ snehasya yas tyāgo viṣayāṇāṃ tathaiva ca rāgadveṣaprahīṇasya tyāgo bhavati nānyathā
english: Renunciation is the giving up of affection and likewise of the objects of sense; for one who has cast off passion and aversion such renunciation comes about, and not otherwise.

sanskrit: āryatā nāma bhūtānāṃ yaḥ karoti prayatnataḥ śubhaṃ karma nirākāro vītarāgatvam eva ca
english: Nobility is that whereby a man strives diligently to do auspicious works for living beings, without thought of self, and to attain freedom from passion.

sanskrit: dhṛtir nāma sukhe duḥkhe yathā nāpnoti vikriyām tāṃ bhajeta sadā prājño ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: Steadfastness is that by which one is not thrown into agitation in pleasure or in pain; let the wise man who desires his own welfare ever cultivate it.

sanskrit: sarvathā kṣamiṇā bhāvyaṃ tathā satyapareṇa ca vītaharṣabhayakrodho dhṛtim āpnoti paṇḍitaḥ
english: In every way one should be forbearing, and likewise devoted to truth; freed from elation, fear, and wrath, the learned man attains steadfastness.

sanskrit: adrohaḥ sarvabhūteṣu karmaṇā manasā girā anugrahaś ca dānaṃ ca satāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Doing no harm to any creature in deed, in thought, or in word, together with kindness and giving—this is the eternal dharma of the good.

sanskrit: ete trayodaśākārāḥ pṛthak satyaikalakṣaṇāḥ bhajante satyam eveha bṛṃhayanti ca bhārata
english: These thirteen forms, though severally bearing the single mark of truth, partake of truth here and make it grow, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nāntaḥ śakyo guṇānāṃ hi vaktuṃ satyasya bhārata ataḥ satyaṃ praśaṃsanti viprāḥ sapitṛdevatāḥ
english: No end can be told of the virtues of truth, O Bhārata; therefore the brahmins, with the ancestors and the gods, praise truth.

sanskrit: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo nānṛtāt pātakaṃ param sthitir hi satyaṃ dharmasya tasmāt satyaṃ na lopayet
english: There is no dharma higher than truth, and no sin greater than falsehood; truth is the very ground on which dharma stands—therefore one should never break truth.

sanskrit: upaiti satyād dānaṃ hi tathā yajñāḥ sadakṣiṇāḥ vratāgnihotraṃ vedāś ca ye cānye dharmaniścayāḥ
english: From truth proceed giving, and sacrifices duly furnished with their fees, the vows and the fire-oblation and the Vedas, and whatever other determinations of dharma there are.

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam aśvamedhasahasrād dhi satyam evātiricyate
english: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were once weighed in the balance; and truth outweighed the thousand horse-sacrifices.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yataḥ prabhavati krodhaḥ kāmaś ca bharatarṣabha śokamohau vivitsā ca parāsutvaṃ tathā madaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whence arise anger and desire, O bull of the Bharatas, grief and delusion, the craving to know, the wish to take another's life, and pride,

sanskrit: lobho mātsaryam īrṣyā ca kutsāsūyā kṛpā tathā etat sarvaṃ mahāprājña yāthātathyena me vada
english: greed, envy, and jealousy, contempt, malice, and likewise pity—all this, O greatly wise one, tell me as it truly is.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca trayodaśaite 'tibalāḥ śatravaḥ prāṇināṃ smṛtāḥ upāsate mahārāja samastāḥ puruṣān iha
english: Bhīṣma said: These thirteen are remembered as the most powerful enemies of living beings; all together they wait upon men here, O great king.

sanskrit: ete pramattaṃ puruṣam apramattā nudanti hi vṛkā iva vilumpanti dṛṣṭvaiva puruṣetarān
english: Themselves never heedless, they assail the heedless man; like wolves they fall upon and rend men less than men the moment they spy them out.

sanskrit: ebhyaḥ pravartate duḥkham ebhyaḥ pāpaṃ pravartate iti martyo vijānīyāt satataṃ bharatarṣabha
english: From these springs suffering, from these springs sin—so let the mortal ever understand, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: eteṣām udayaṃ sthānaṃ kṣayaṃ ca puruṣottama hanta te vartayiṣyāmi tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Their rising, their seat, and their destruction, O best of men—come, I shall expound to you; listen as I declare it.

sanskrit: lobhāt krodhaḥ prabhavati paradoṣair udīryate kṣamayā tiṣṭhate rājañ śrīmāṃś ca vinivartate
english: From greed arises anger; it is roused by the faults of others; through forbearance it is held in check, O king, and in a man of dignity it turns away.

sanskrit: saṃkalpāj jāyate kāmaḥ sevyamāno vivardhate avadyadarśanād vyeti tattvajñānāc ca dhīmatām
english: From resolve is born desire; indulged, it grows; it departs at the sight of its baseness, and through knowledge of reality it departs from the wise.

sanskrit: viruddhāni hi śāstrāṇi paśyantīhālpabuddhayaḥ vivitsā jāyate tatra tattvajñānān nivartate
english: Men of little understanding see the scriptures here at variance with one another; thereupon the craving to know is born, which turns back through knowledge of reality.

sanskrit: prīteḥ śokaḥ prabhavati viyogāt tasya dehinaḥ yadā nirarthakaṃ vetti tadā sadyaḥ praṇaśyati
english: From love springs grief, at the parting from its object for the embodied one; when he knows it to be empty of purpose, then at once it perishes.

sanskrit: parāsutā krodhalobhād abhyāsāc ca pravartate dayayā sarvabhūtānāṃ nirvedāt sā nivartate
english: The wish to take another's life proceeds from anger and greed and from habit; through compassion toward all beings and through detachment it turns away.

sanskrit: sattvatyāgāt tu mātsaryam ahitāni ca sevate etat tu kṣīyate tāta sādhūnām upasevanāt
english: From the abandonment of goodness springs envy, and it courts what is harmful; but this, dear son, is worn away by attendance upon the good.

sanskrit: kulāj jñānāt tathaiśvaryān mado bhavati dehinām ebhir eva tu vijñātair madaḥ sadyaḥ praṇaśyati
english: From high birth, from learning, and from lordship comes the pride of embodied beings; but when these very things are rightly understood, pride at once perishes.

sanskrit: īrṣyā kāmāt prabhavati saṃgharṣāc caiva bhārata itareṣāṃ tu martyānāṃ prajñayā sā praṇaśyati
english: Jealousy arises from desire and from rivalry, O Bhārata; but in mortals of another sort it perishes through wisdom.

sanskrit: vibhramāl lokabāhyānāṃ dveṣyair vākyair asaṃgataiḥ kutsā saṃjāyate rājann upekṣābhiḥ praśāmyati
english: From the wanderings of those who stand outside the world, and from hateful, ill-fitting words, contempt is born, O king; through indifference it is stilled.

sanskrit: pratikartum aśakyāya balasthāyāpakāriṇe asūyā jāyate tīvrā kāruṇyād vinivartate
english: Toward a wrongdoer entrenched in power, against whom one is unable to retaliate, fierce malice is born; through compassion it turns away.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇān satataṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ saṃjāyate kṛpā dharmaniṣṭhāṃ yadā vetti tadā śāmyati sā kṛpā
english: Seeing the wretched again and again, thereupon pity is born; but when one knows their steadfastness in dharma, then that pity is stilled.

sanskrit: etāny eva jitāny āhuḥ praśamāc ca trayodaśa ete hi dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ sarve doṣās trayodaśa tvayā sarvātmanā nityaṃ vijitā jeṣyase ca tān
english: These thirteen, they say, are conquered through tranquility; and these same thirteen faults were all those of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. By you, with your whole soul and ever, they have been conquered, and you shall conquer them still.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ānṛśaṃsyaṃ vijānāmi darśanena satāṃ sadā nṛśaṃsān na vijānāmi teṣāṃ karma ca bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I know gentleness by the constant sight of the good; the cruel I do not know, nor their deeds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kaṇṭakān kūpam agniṃ ca varjayanti yathā narāḥ tathā nṛśaṃsakarmāṇaṃ varjayanti narā naram
english: As men shun thorns, a pit, and fire, so do men shun the man whose deeds are cruel.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃso hy adhamo nityaṃ pretya ceha ca bhārata tasmād bravīhi kauravya tasya dharmaviniścayam
english: For the cruel man is ever the lowest, both hereafter and here, O Bhārata; therefore, O Kaurava, tell me the settled judgment of dharma concerning him.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca spṛhāsyāntarhitā caiva viditārthā ca karmaṇā ākroṣṭā kruśyate caiva bandhitā badhyate ca yaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: He whose craving is hidden away yet betrayed by his deeds; who reviles and is reviled in turn, who binds others and is himself bound;

sanskrit: dattānukīrtir viṣamaḥ kṣudro naikṛtikaḥ śaṭhaḥ asaṃbhogī ca mānī ca tathā saṅgī vikatthanaḥ
english: who proclaims his own gifts, who is crooked, mean, deceitful, treacherous; who shares nothing, is proud, attached, and boastful;

sanskrit: sarvātiśaṅkī paruṣo bāliśaḥ kṛpaṇas tathā vargapraśaṃsī satatam āśramadveṣasaṃkarī
english: who suspects everyone, is harsh, foolish, and miserly; who forever flatters his own faction, who hates and confounds the orders of life—
